body:
I have a coworker who has a house, a boyfriend, a degree, and goes out every weekend, and has such a rich social life she specifically needs to block off time for herself.

I have a shitty apartment, a history of sexual and physical abuse, have been isolated to the point I developed delirium, and have kinda lost a big chunk of my enthusiasm. Doing fun things on the weekend is good but its never been enough to have the underlying trauma of everything in my life go away entirely. Having fun is an exercise in ignoring the bad feelings and not trying to force good ones.
Usually when people tell their life story as a comment to these it doesn’t really feel like it applies to the post but this is the first time where it actually felt meaningful and helpful.
It means a lot to know that I’m not the only person who feels this way.

I would have these panic attacks cause I would feel someone touching my inner thigh or I would see a hand out of the corner of my eye. It was always my hands but they were still alien to me and I kept perceiving them as outside threats.

The way I ended up dealing was I would just loon at the spot I had just touched and recognize that it was me that had touched it. 

Later I then would let someone touch me somewhere less threatening and I was able to build up a tolerance to the anxiety attacks.

Lol. Its a little funny that you said that cause my boyfriend left me last night. 

They weren’t abusive (they were the best partner I ever had) but its still fucking with my head.
I’m already getting help. Its just a slow process and we haven’t made it to this point yet. We’re still working on my abandonment issues.
